newsitem.title: USA: Feingold wants independent counsel on fundraising.
newsitem.headline: Feingold wants independent counsel on fundraising.

text.p: Sen. Russell Feingold, the Democratic sponsor of a sweeping campaign finance reform bill, said on Sunday he supported appointing an independent counsel to probe U.S. political fund-raising.

"Regrettably, I think we've come to the point where, under the discretionary powers of the attorney general, we probably do have to go to a special counsel," Feingold, a Wisconsin Democrat, said on NBC's "Meet the Press" programme.

Feingold was joined in his approval of an independent counsel by the campaign finance bill's co-sponsor Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, as well as Sen. Mitch McConnell, a Kentucky Republican who heads his party's senatorial fund-raising efforts.
Former Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot and former Democratic Sen. Bill Bradley of New Jersey also said an independent counsel was warranted.
A White House spokeswoman Sunday declined comment on Feingold's call for an independent counsel.

The McCain-Feingold bill provides incentives for candidates to adhere to voluntary spending limits and bans soft money contributions, which are now unregulated, and contributions from political action committees.
President Bill Clinton has urged Congress to pass the measure.
